elements.requirement: Information to which a request relates is exempt information if it constitutes personal data of which the applicant is the data subject.
elements.quote: exempt information if it constitutes personal data of which the applicant is the data subject

elements.requirement: Information to which a request relates is exempt information if it constitutes personal data not relating to the applicant as data subject and the first, second, or third statutory condition is satisfied.
elements.quote: exempt information if— (a) it constitutes personal data which does not fall within subsection (1), and (b) the first, second or third condition below is satisfied

elements.requirement: The first condition is satisfied where disclosure of the personal data to a member of the public otherwise than under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 would contravene any of the data protection principles, or would do so if the exemptions for manual unstructured data held by public authorities in section 24(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 were disregarded.
elements.quote: The first condition is that the disclosure of the information to a member of the public otherwise than under this Act— (a) would contravene any of the data protection principles, or (b) would do so if the exemptions in section 24(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 (manual unstructured data held by public authorities) were disregarded

elements.requirement: The second condition is satisfied where disclosure of the personal data to a member of the public otherwise than under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 would contravene Article 21 of the UK GDPR concerning the right to object to processing.
elements.quote: The second condition is that the disclosure of the information to a member of the public otherwise than under this Act would contravene Article 21 of the UK GDPR (general processing: right to object to processing)

elements.requirement: The third condition is satisfied where, on an access request under Article 15(1) of the UK GDPR, the information would be withheld under section 15, 16, or 26 of, or Schedule 2, 3, or 4 to, the Data Protection Act 2018, or on a request under section 45(1)(b) of that Act, the information would be withheld under section 45(4) or 78A of that Act.
elements.quote: The third condition is that— (a) on a request under Article 15(1) of the UK GDPR (general processing: right of access by the data subject) for access to personal data, the information would be withheld in reliance on provision made by or under section 15, 16 or 26 of, or Schedule 2, 3 or 4 to, the Data Protection Act 2018, or (b) on a request under section 45(1)(b) of that Act (law enforcement processing: right of access by the data subject), the information would be withheld in reliance on section 45(4) or 78A of that Act

elements.requirement: A public authority's duty to confirm or deny does not arise in relation to information that is, or if held would be, exempt personal data of which the applicant is the data subject.
elements.quote: The duty to confirm or deny does not arise in relation to information which is (or if it were held by the public authority would be) exempt information by virtue of subsection (1)

elements.requirement: A public authority's duty to confirm or deny does not arise in relation to other information if giving the confirmation or denial to a member of the public would, apart from the Freedom of Information Act 2000, contravene any of the data protection principles, or would do so if the section 24(1) Data Protection Act 2018 exemptions were disregarded.
elements.quote: giving a member of the public the confirmation or denial that would have to be given to comply with section 1(1)(a)— (i) would (apart from this Act) contravene any of the data protection principles, or (ii) would do so if the exemptions in section 24(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 (manual unstructured data held by public authorities) were disregarded

elements.requirement: A public authority's duty to confirm or deny does not arise in relation to other information if giving the confirmation or denial to a member of the public would, apart from the Freedom of Information Act 2000, contravene Article 21 of the UK GDPR.
elements.quote: giving a member of the public the confirmation or denial that would have to be given to comply with section 1(1)(a) would (apart from this Act) contravene Article 21 of the UK GDPR (general processing: right to object to processing)

elements.requirement: A public authority's duty to confirm or deny does not arise in relation to other information if, on a request under Article 15(1) of the UK GDPR for confirmation of processing, the information would be withheld in reliance on section 15, 16, or 26 of, or Schedule 2, 3, or 4 to, the Data Protection Act 2018.
elements.quote: on a request under Article 15(1) of the UK GDPR (general processing: right of access by the data subject) for confirmation of whether personal data is being processed, the information would be withheld in reliance on a provision listed in subsection (4A)(a)

elements.requirement: A public authority's duty to confirm or deny does not arise in relation to other information if, on a request under section 45(1)(a) of the Data Protection Act 2018, the information would be withheld in reliance on section 45(4) or 78A of that Act.
elements.quote: on a request under section 45(1)(a) of the Data Protection Act 2018 (law enforcement processing: right of access by the data subject), the information would be withheld in reliance on section 45(4) or 78A of that Act

elements.requirement: The data protection principles are defined as the principles set out in Article 5(1) of the UK GDPR and section 34(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018.
elements.quote: “the data protection principles” means the principles set out in— Article 5(1) of the UK GDPR, andsection 34(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018

elements.requirement: The term 'data subject' has the same meaning as in section 3 of the Data Protection Act 2018.
elements.quote: “data subject” has the same meaning as in the Data Protection Act 2018 (see section 3 of that Act)

elements.requirement: The terms 'personal data' and 'processing' have the same meaning as in Parts 5 to 7 of the Data Protection Act 2018.
elements.quote: “personal data” and “processing” have the same meaning as in Parts 5 to 7 of the Data Protection Act 2018 (see section 3(2), (4) and (14) of that Act)

elements.requirement: The term 'the UK GDPR' has the same meaning as in Parts 5 to 7 of the Data Protection Act 2018.
elements.quote: “the UK GDPR” has the same meaning as in Parts 5 to 7 of the Data Protection Act 2018 (see section 3(10) and (14) of that Act)

elements.requirement: When determining whether disclosure of information would contravene the lawfulness principle in Article 5(1)(a) of the UK GDPR, Article 6(1) of the UK GDPR is to be read as if its second sub-paragraph disapplied only the gateway in point (ea) relating to recognised legitimate interests.
elements.quote: Article 6(1) of the UK GDPR (lawfulness) is to be read as if the second sub-paragraph (disapplying the legitimate interests gateways in relation to public authorities) disapplied only the gateway in point (ea) (recognised legitimate interests)
